newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms, liquidity eases.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms, liquidity eases.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in slow late trading on Wednesday, with liquidity seen easing in the afternoon, dealers said.
They said overnight money fell to 9.5 percent in the afternoon from a high of 17.0/18.0 percent in the morning.
Overnight and tom/next swap were last offered at 0.65 and 0.55 points, respectively. Dealers said short-dated swap rates were seen trending down on anticipation of improved liquidity.
They said offshore players seemed to continue to favour the rupiah, keeping it consistently traded at the higher end of the central bank's intervention band.
One U.S. bank dealer said foreign players were seen selling dollars below the 2,346.0 level shortly before the fixing which were happily taken up by local players.
"We think the central bank might have at least absorbed some $500 million from the market today," the dealer said.
But confirmation was not immediately available.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,345.80/46.30 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,346.0/46.75.
Dealers were unclear of any specific reason behind the selling or whether offshore operators were still speculating for another band widening in the short-term.
"We do not believe there will be any widening in the near future. We were happy to buy from offshore below the 2,346 level and sold it to the central bank later," another foreign bank dealer said.
The dealer said offshore selling might be linked to the active stock market in the past few days which seemed to have received some fresh capital inflows.
Dealers said operators seemed to anticipate ample liquidity conditions on Thursday and Friday following a large amount of dollar buying by the central bank on Tuesday and Wednesday.
However, trading was slow and operators seemed to be reluctant to deal aggressively as the year-end approached.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,345.0/45.5 and 2,344.35/45.60, respectively.
The U.S. bank dealer said if the expected flush liquidity extended into next week and the central bank kept its three- to four-point depreciation policy, the dollar might rebound.
He said the current expensive swap costs dented operators from going long in dollars. Dealers said easing of short-term rates helped bring longer-term rates down.
One-month swap declined to 15.5/16.0 from 16.5/17.5, two to 30.75/31.50 from 32.0/34.0, three to 43.5/44.5 from 45.0/46.5 and six to 87.5/88.5 from 88.5/90.0 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,346/2,538 and the converison band to 2,346/2,394 on Wednesday.
